evidence: Cic. Off. 2.43: vēra glōria, opposed to ficta
Cic. Verr. 2.4.147: vērus ac germānus Metellus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Opposed to fictus and falsus; the same word as for “true”.

terms.gloss: genuine, real, true to its name
evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.97: illī veterēs germānīque Campānī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly “of the same parents”; in the sense “genuine”, a favourite of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).
Late Latin for “active, practical”; it never means “actual, real”. Say vērus, or rē vērā for “actually” (see actually).

phrases.latin: Castella Theodōrus ex tessellīs magnēticīs aedificāre solēbat; castellum vērum numquam vīderat.
phrases.english: Theo used to build castles out of magnetic tiles; he had never seen a real castle.

phrases.latin: «Euax! Dracō est! Dracō vērus, tata!» «Dracō marīnus, hippocamporum cōnsanguineus. Vērus.»
phrases.english: “Wow! It’s a dragon! A real dragon, Dad!” “A sea dragon, a cousin of the sea horses. A real one.”
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.latin: vēra glōria rādīcēs agit atque etiam prōpāgātur, ficta omnia celeriter tamquam flōsculī dēcidunt
phrases.english: real glory puts down roots and even spreads; everything fake drops quickly, like little blossoms

sources: Lewis & Short: verus · Lewis & Short: germanus

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
